stories.title: Death toll from Russian strike on Kyiv depot rises to 37
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on a depot containing explosive objects near Kyiv has risen to 37, the region's governor said. "Unfortunately, the number of dead in the Bucha district has risen to 37... Rescuers and all relevant services are continuing their operations at the scene of the tragedy," Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko said on Telegram. Earlier, 27 people were reported to have been killed after a Russian drone struck a warehouse near Kyiv's western suburbs overnight, sparking a huge fire and explosions. The warehouse appeared to have been storing "explosive objects", Ukrainian prosecutors said, opening an investigation into criminal negligence.

stories.summary: Energy has been identified as the principal contributor to rising business costs by an advisory forum established by the Government. The Cost of Business Advisory Forum has issued its final report setting out 63 recommendations to boost competitiveness and cut costs. The report found that the Government should consider the feasibility of a new scheme to reduce prices for large energy intensive business users. It also highlighted the importance of price transparency and easier switching for non-domestic customers.

stories.title: Fed has 'work to do' if above-target inflation remains
stories.summary: The US Federal Reserve will "have work to do" if policymakers are not confident that underlying inflation is returning to its 2% target, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said today. His remarks acknowledged that financial conditions do not appear restrictive and marked the closest he has come to acknowledging interest rate hikes may be needed to ease price pressures. "Here is my standard - we must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do. That's our job ... our mandate ... and our charge to keep," Warsh said in a remarks prepared for delivery to the Fed's Jackson Hole economic symposium in Wyoming. While much of the 16-page address focused on large issues, like the influence of artificial intelligence, that Warsh feels will be critical in the long run, it also included some key acknowledgements - including that "short-term interest rates are the predominant tool to achieve the dual mandate."

stories.title: Over 2,400 missing after deadly Nepal, China floods
stories.summary: The number of people missing in Nepal and China leapt to more than 2,400, underscoring the scale of the disaster days after a tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept away villages and killed hundreds. Rescuers were battling through mud even as the threat of new floods loomed, with emergency teams recovering 584 bodies so far - and some of the dead swept downstream as far away as India. The new figures came as Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing list already including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash. Two Irish citizens, who have been named by the Nepalese Tourism Department as 46-year-old Santosh Sahu and 18-year-old Spandan Sahu, are among those missing.

stories.title: Bannigan steps down as Monaghan boss as 'goalposts move'
stories.summary: Gabriel Bannigan has stepped down as Monaghan manager after two seasons in charge of the Oriel County citing moving goalposts. The Aughnamullen man replaced Vinny Corey in late September 2024 and his coaching ticket in Year 1 included Andy Moran, who went on to manage Mayo to All-Ireland glory this season, with a Division 2 title the highlight. Despite suffering relegation from Division 1 this season, Monaghan bounced back to have an excellent Ulster campaign. Jack McCarron's extra-time forcing side-line against Derry in the semi-final was one of the moments of the year while they also took eventual champions Armagh to extra-time in the provincial final.

stories.title: The new FAI National League: All you need to know
stories.summary: CK United v Newbridge Town, SETU Carlow Sports Campus, 2pm (Group 3) This Saturday, the new FAI National League will kick off around the country with 15 clubs involved in a truncated inaugural season that will run across the autumn. While colloquially referred to as a third tier, it's not officially part of the men's League of Ireland which is currently made up of the SSE Airtricity Men's Premier Division and the SSE Airtricity Men's First Division. Promotion and relegation exists between those two tiers but in this initial season at least, teams will not be able to go up from the FAI National League into the First Division or vice versa.

stories.title: Erasmus reverses two of his changes for All Blacks Test
stories.summary: South Africa have made two late changes to their team ahead of Saturday's second Test against New Zealand in Cape Town, with Rassie Erasmus drafting Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Cheslin Kolbe back into his side. Out-half Feinberg-Mngomezulu had initially been dropped after a disappointing performance in last week’s 33-16 defeat in Johannesburg, with Handre Pollard slated to start in the 10 shirt when Erasmus named his team on Monday. However, a calf strain has since ruled Pollard out of action this week, with Stormers out-half Feinberg-Mngomezulu restored, and Manie Libbok named on the bench. The Springboks head coach has also put Kolbe back into his team to replace Kurt-Lee Arendse. Kolbe limped off during the second half of last week’s defeat and had initially been ruled out by the South African coaching team, but the 32-year-old has now been deemed fit to play.

stories.title: Who are pop idols Katseye and why have 2 of them gone on hiatus?
stories.summary: Freelance journalist and broadcaster, writing about music and the arts. One of the most sought-after event tickets this summer has not been for the All-Ireland final, Katie Taylor's Croke Park retirement fight or the long sold-out Electric Picnic, but for the debut Irish performance by Katseye - the latest pop phenomenon to sweep the globe. Irish parents’ WhatsApp groups have descended into panicked meltdowns in search of tickets for the girl group’s gig in Dublin on September 1st, when they will kick off their 'WildWorld’ tour at the 3Arena. Tickets were snapped up within minutes of going on sale back in May: girl groups, as we’ve learned from the popularity of Blackpink, Twice, FLO, Girlset and Say Now, are big business in 2026. It’s akin to Beliebers, Directioners or Lady Gaga’s Little Monsters; Gen Z music fans may recognise elements of the aforementioned Blinks (Blackpink), Swifties (Taylor Swift) or BTS (Army) in the mania surrounding the pop band, whose fans are known as Eyekons. The Los Angeles-based six-piece have become a phenomenon since their formation in 2023, when they were drawn together via an online X Factor-style reality show called Dream Academy (a Netflix documentary about the year-long process was released in 2024). The show, which was launched on YouTube and Weverse, the South Korean fan community platform, was a collaboration between South Korean record label Hybe (the conglomerate behind the unparalleled success of K-Pop boyband BTS) and Geffen Records. The goal? Create a K-Pop-oriented pop group with a Western production style.

stories.title: How can you spot a liar? An expert weighs in
stories.summary: With a new season of The Traitors Ireland this Sunday, 30 August, Dr Sabina Brennan, Psychologist & Neuroscientist, joined Drivetime to discuss why we lie and whether you can spot a liar. We've all heard you can spot a liar by their tells: scratching their nose, breaking eye contact, tripping over their words or changing their voice. In theory, we should be able to notice when they're being deceitful because they will start acting abnormally. But Brennan explains that these tells are mostly "myths". In reality, lying is a "natural ability", she says. "I think the important thing to remember about The Traitors is that it's a game, so it's not about people necessarily becoming dishonest. They've accepted a temporary role in which deception is permitted, and it's expected, and it's even rewarded.

stories.title: Poor weather hampers rescue operations in Nepal
stories.summary: Nepal has suspended search and rescue due to bad weather and said it needs foreign technical help to cope with the devastating flood that tore through an area bordering Tibet. The Himalayan nation of 30 million people will also need about $4 billion to $5 billion to rebuild after the destruction caused by the flood on Wednesday, the finance minister told Reuters. Triggered by a glacier collapse, the huge torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris hurtled through mountain river systems, killing at least 626 people in Nepal and seven in China's Tibet as it destroyed buildings, bridges and power stations in its path. Nearly 3,000 people are still missing - about 2,426 in Nepal and at least 554 in Tibet's Gyirong County - including at least 540 foreign nationals, many of them Hindu pilgrims from India.

stories.title: Mortgage approvals reached 15-year monthly high in July
stories.summary: Mortgage approvals reached their highest monthly levels in at least 15 years in July, latest figures from Banking & Payments Federation Ireland (BPFI) show. BPFI said first-time buyers (FTBs) continued to drive approvals, accounting for over half (3,575) of the 6,253 mortgages approved during the month. The total number of approvals was 14.4% higher than July 2025. Those remortgaging and switchers made up one fifth of all approvals - which was a 71.6% rise on last year.

stories.title: Public pressure forced fuel excise duty shift - Sinn Féin
stories.summary: Sinn Féin's Pearse Doherty has said the Government's move to delay the phasing out of cuts to excise duty on petrol and diesel was the result of public pressure. The cuts were introduced in April following nationwide fuel protests after the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East sent fuel prices soaring. "There is no way that Sinn Féin will stand by and allow that to happen when these fuels prices are increased," he said, noting that - once the temporary cuts have been removed - the price of diesel will increase by 34 cent a litre and petrol by 29 cent. Mr Doherty said Sinn Féin would bring forward an amendment in the Dáil tomorrow calling for no further tax increases on petrol and diesel while fuel prices remain high.

stories.title: 7 ways to minimise dark circles at home
stories.summary: Dark circles are one of the most prolific skin concerns across all ages, and can be down to a myriad of reasons ranging from alcohol to hormones to lack of sleep or simply genetics. "Dark circles are slightly misleading because they are not really one condition," explains aesthetic practitioner Dr David Jack. "What we perceive as darkness underneath the eyes can come from increased melanin in the skin, visible blood vessels through very thin eyelid skin, changes in the underlying anatomy that create shadow or sometimes a mixture of all three." The colour can offer some indication of the cause. Jack says brownish circles are more suggestive of pigmentation, while blue, purple or reddish tones can indicate a greater vascular component.

stories.summary: Voters in Iceland are taking part in a referendum on whether or not to revive membership talks with the European Union, more than a decade after they were frozen. The coalition government brought forward the referendum following US President Donald Trump's threat to seize nearby Greenland. Polling stations opened at 9am local time and will close at 10pm, with the first indications expected before midnight. The campaign has been incredibly tight, with tiny margins for both the 'No' and 'Yes' camps. The latest Gallup poll put the No side ahead with 51.6% of the vote.

stories.title: Foreign Affairs Dept spent almost €17,000 for Davos hotel
stories.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs spent almost €17,000 on accommodation for the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Switzerland and nearly €15,000 on flights for a diplomat and family members posted overseas. The department also ran up an accommodation bill of just under €13,000 for hotel rooms during the COP30 climate conference in Brazil and paid over €7,000 for an 18-night stay at a swish New York hotel. The nightly cost of the room in New York was close to €400 for a staff member to stay at the four-star Shelburne Sonesta during the UN General Assembly. In total, the department spent almost €4.2m on flights last year with a further €2.58m paid for hotels and accommodation.

stories.title: Coughlan: I'm not Mourinho, it's all down to the players
stories.summary: Waterford manager Graham Coughlan put his team's resurgence under his guidance down to the attitude of his players after their 2-0 away win against St Patrick's Athletic in Inchicore. Second-half goals from Jorgen Voilas and John Mahon powered Waterford to victory in Richmond Park, propelling them that much closer to safety and wounding St Pat's title prospects just when it looked like Shamrock Rovers' form was faltering. The result encapsulated the turnaround that Coughlan has inspired in Waterford since taking over as manager in May. His first game in charge had been in this fixture, his side well beaten 4-1 by Pat's with Coughlan afterwards lamenting their inability to get the basics right. At that stage, Waterford were rooted to the bottom of the table on six points, with no wins from their first 14 league games.

stories.title: Cian O'Neill appointed head coach of Cork hurlers
stories.summary: Cian O'Neill has been appointment head coach of the Cork hurlers as the Rebels continue to shake up their management team following another disappointing end to a championship season. O'Neill left the Kerry football coaching staff following their All-Ireland defeat to Mayo and has previously been involved with the Cork footballers. The Kildare man, who is based in Cork, was last involved with a hurling squad back in 2011 when he was strength and conditioning coach with Tipperary - winning a Liam MacCarthy cup a year previous, in 2010. O'Neill has previously been involved with Cork manager Ben O'Connor's home club, Newtownshandrum, with whom he helped win the 2009 Munster Club Championship before losing to Ballyhale Shamrocks in the All-Ireland final.
